title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — Table 4: Expenses Summary (p.46)
key_points: Table 4 逐项列示费用同比变动：Total expenses 2022 年 $41,095M，较 2021 年增加 $7,985M，增幅 24%。
Card Member rewards +$2,995M（+27%）；Business development +$1,181M（+31%）；Card Member services +$966M（+48%）；Marketing +$167M（+3%）；Salaries and employee benefits +$1,012M（+16%）；Other, net +$1,664M（+35%）。
Card Member rewards 增长主要来自 Membership Rewards 与 cash back 合计约 $2.0B、cobrand rewards 约 $1.0B，均由 billed business 增长驱动。
Business development 增长主要来自 partner payments 与 client incentives，均由 network volumes 增长驱动。
Other expenses 增长主要由于当年 Amex Ventures 投资出现净亏损，而上年为净收益。

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Executive Overview: expense behavior (p.43)
key_points: Amex 明确说明 Card Member rewards、Card Member services 与 Business development 三类费用「generally correlated to volumes or are variable based on usage」，即与业务量挂钩或随使用量变动，而非固定销货成本。
上述三类费用同比增长由 network volume 增长与 travel-related benefits 使用量上升驱动。
Card Member rewards 增长还因 billed business 中 travel 等可获增量奖励的类别占比上升。
Operating expenses 同比增长 24%，主要由于当年 Amex Ventures 股权投资净亏损（上年为净收益）以及为支持业务增长而扩大员工规模带来的薪酬成本上升。
公司维持 CET1 资本比率在 10%–11% 目标区间内。
raw_excerpt: Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or are variable based on usage, and increased year-over year due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits. Card Member rewards expense growth was also driven by a larger proportion of billed business in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel. … Operating expenses increased 24 percent year-over-year, primarily driven by net losses in the current year associated with our Amex Ventures equity investments as compared to net gains in the prior year, as well as higher compensation costs

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A consolidated EXPENSES narrative (p.52)
key_points: 合并层面费用增长归因：Card Member rewards 与 Card Member services 是主要驱动项。
Card Member rewards 增长源于 billed business 上升，以及 travel 等可获增量奖励类别的支出占比提高、travel 相关兑换占比提高。
Business development 增长源于 billed business 上升带来的 partner payments 增加。
Card Member services 增长源于 travel-related benefits 使用量上升。
Marketing 增长源于推动增长动能与加速新卡获取的业务投入。
Salaries and employee benefits 与 other expenses 增长源于薪酬成本与服务成本上升。
raw_excerpt: Total expenses increased, primarily driven by higher Card Member rewards expense and Card Member services expense. Card Member rewards expense increased, primarily driven by higher billed business and a larger proportion of spend in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel … Business development expense increased, primarily due to increased partner payments driven by higher billed business … Card Member services expense increased, primarily driven by higher usage of travel-related benefits.

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — Capital Resources: Basel III ratios and SCB (p.13)
key_points: 公司与 AENB 须分别维持 CET1、Tier 1、Total capital 比率不低于 4.5%、6.0%、8.0%。
2022 年 8 月 4 日美联储确认公司 stress capital buffer (SCB) 为 2.5%，与 2021 年 6 月公布水平一致。
计入 SCB 后，公司有效最低比率为 CET1 7.0%、Tier 1 8.5%、Total capital 10.5%。
公司作为 Category IV 机构，采用 Basel III 标准化方法计算风险加权资产，不适用 advanced approaches。
raw_excerpt: The Company and AENB must each maintain CET1 capital, Tier 1 capital and Total capital ratios of at least 4.5 percent, 6.0 percent and 8.0 percent, respectively … On August 4, 2022, the Federal Reserve confirmed the SCB for the Company of 2.5 percent, which remained unchanged from the level announced in June 2021. As a result, the effective minimum ratios for the Company … are 7.0 percent, 8.5 percent and 10.5 percent for the CET1 capital, Tier 1 capital and Total capital ratios, respectively.

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — Glossary of Selected Terminology (p.82)
key_points: 10-K 设有「GLOSSARY OF SELECTED TERMINOLOGY」，对非 GAAP 指标明确标注（如 Adjusted net interest income 被标注为 non-GAAP measure）。
该术语表中未出现 gross margin 或 gross profit 的定义条目。
Adjusted net interest income 定义为归属于 Card Member loans 的净利息收入（GAAP 下含视为不可收回的利息），剔除不归属于 Card Member loans 的利息费用与利息收入。
raw_excerpt: GLOSSARY OF SELECTED TERMINOLOGY — Adjusted net interest income — A non-GAAP measure that represents net interest income attributable to our Card Member loans (which includes, on a GAAP basis, interest that is deemed uncollectible), excluding the impact of interest expense and interest income not attributable to our Card Member loans.

raw_excerpt: The foreign currency adjusted information assumes a constant exchange rate between the periods being compared for purposes of currency translation into U.S. dollars … FX-adjusted revenues is a non GAAP measure. We believe the presentation of information on a foreign currency adjusted basis is helpful to investors by making it easier to compare our performance in one period to that of another period without the variability caused by fluctuations in currency exchange rates.

title: American Express FY2022 10-K — Business Environment (MD&A overview of FY2022 results)
key_points: Spending on the network reached record levels in 2022, and credit metrics remained below pre-pandemic levels.

Commercial Services billed business grew 21% YoY, reflecting U.S. SME growth and continued steady recovery in spending by U.S. large and global corporate clients.
International billed business grew 23% YoY (36% FX-adjusted).

Service fees and other revenues increased 36%, driven in part by higher travel-related revenues.
Net interest income increased 28%, primarily driven by growth in Card Member loans.

Card Member loans increased 22% YoY, with the majority of growth from existing Card Members; billed business growth began to moderate toward year end as the company lapped the steep phase of recovery.
Provisions for credit losses increased versus the prior year, reflecting a reserve build of $617 million compared with a reserve release of $2.5 billion in the prior year.

Net income was $7.5 billion ($9.85 per share) vs $8.1 billion ($10.02 per share) a year ago; the reduction reflected credit reserve builds and net losses in the Amex Ventures portfolio in 2022 versus sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in that portfolio in 2021.

American Express Company Tier 1 capital ratio was 11.1% and Total capital ratio was 12.8%.
American Express Company Tier 1 leverage ratio was 9.9% against an effective minimum of 4.0%.
American Express National Bank CET1 was 11.3%, Tier 1 11.3%, Total 13.2% and Tier 1 leverage 9.7%.
Risk-weighted assets were $194.4B and average total assets used for the Tier 1 leverage ratio were $218.6B.
Common Equity Tier 1 capital was $20.0B and Tier 1 capital $21.6B.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Table 9: U.S. Consumer Services segment selected income statement data
key_points: USCS total revenues net of interest expense were $23,914M in 2022 vs $18,922M in 2021, up 26%.
USCS total expenses were $17,493M in 2022 vs $13,883M in 2021, up 26%.
USCS pretax segment income was $5,400M in 2022 vs $5,958M in 2021, down 9%.
USCS provisions for credit losses were $1,021M in 2022 vs $(919)M in 2021.
USCS net interest income was $7,474M in 2022 vs $5,933M in 2021, up 26%.
USCS billed business was $553.0B in 2022 vs $444.2B in 2021, up 24%.
USCS net write-off rate (principal, interest and fees) was 1.1% in 2022 and 1.1% in 2021, versus 2.9% in 2020.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 18: Service Fees and Other Revenue and Other Expenses detail

Data processing and equipment expense was $2,606M in 2022 vs $2,431M in 2021; professional services $2,074M vs $1,958M.
